newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish bonds end higher, underperform Italy.
newsitem.headline: Spanish bonds end higher, underperform Italy.

text.p: Spain's debt market ended higher on Wednesday, although it underperformed Italy's Btp, as dealers adopted a more positive attitude toward future EU talks, from France-German meeting on Friday to the EU Amsterdam summit.
"Now the basic idea is Amsterdam's summit will solve all the tensions. And the rule of thumb is easy -- buy on EMU, sell on no EMU," said a trader at All Trading in Madrid.
Others added the latest rally in peripheral markets was mainly a knee-jerk reaction to the recent selling pressure.
"Yesterday and today we mainly had short covering," said Jose Ramon Arechederra at ABN Amro in Madrid.
The short end of the yield curve, well supported today by a rebounding peseta, was closely watching the domestic economy.
On Friday, the focus will be the release of May CPI, that official forecasts said should be running at 1.5 percent year on year, down from 1.7 percent in April.

Although a part of the market still thinks that such a historical low level of inflation should prompt the Bank of Spain in its fifth cut of the official rate in the year by 25 basis points to 5.00 perce, others disagree.
"I think the central bank can't risk it," a dealer said.
